correctness.rationale: For each vertex the recursive A_v exactly enumerates ancestor antichains by splitting on whether the root is included. Every non-antichain GP subset has a unique selected ancestor p and a unique child v such that all other selected vertices form a nonempty antichain of T_v; the reverse construction is valid because comparable selected descendants would put three vertices on one geodesic. Disjoint weighted enumeration gives Gamma_T=A_r+sum_{p->v} z_p(A_v-1) for every finite nonempty tree and arbitrary root. The actual verify.py tests direct BFS/geodesic subsets on 1,692 trees, independent recurrences, alternative roots, weights, and a known broom formula. Finite checks are not substituted for the bijective proof.

originality.rationale: A complete, vertex-weighted polynomial for all finite trees is derived from a unique antichain-plus-parent-edge decomposition. The founding 2024 article already gives a universal inclusion–exclusion prescription over known maximal general-position sets; it does not supply this direct efficient rooted formula. Its path/broom instances are included but cannot entail the all-tree symbolic identity without a further tree-specific theorem. Searches for equivalent antichain, convex-independence, and geodesic formulations produced no actual stronger matching statement. Remaining risk is an unindexed equivalence; search non-retrieval is not treated as proof.
residual_risks: An earlier theorem under another term (for instance antichain polynomials or geodesic convex independence) may imply the same expansion and was not located.
Some related papers were assessed only through abstracts; absence of a matching claim cannot be certified from those snippets.

The general inclusion–exclusion identity in the 2024 article is formally valid for every graph; distinguishing the direct weighted polynomial-time tree formula is the substantive novelty claim, not discovery of computability.
No independent originality audit or expert validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The complete general-position polynomial is a motivated graph invariant, and this theorem provides all degrees and the full multivariate weight profile on every tree by a linear-size algebraic circuit and efficient coefficient recursion. The decomposition is structural and extends beyond previously enumerated graph families; it is neither a thin parameter slice nor a routine scalar-number recomputation. Arbitrary tree shapes and vertex weights are covered.
